paragraphs: By way of introduction, my name is Joshua Chappell. My intent is to apply for the HVAC Service Technician position at [Company]. I am making a career change into the skilled trades, and I want to be straight with you about where I stand.

I do not have three years of HVAC experience. What I have is seven years of running my own field service business, and the habits that came with it. I scheduled my own jobs, drove to the site, handled the customer at the door, and finished the work. I held 5.0-star reviews for over an entire year and delivered 98% of my projects on time. I have spent years working on construction, trades, and industrial job sites, so ladders, attics, rooftops, and hauling 50 to 75 pounds of gear are normal parts of my day. I stewarded a $30,000 equipment inventory as a teacher and kept $1 million of technical equipment running in the field at Grand Canyon Education. I also spent two years teaching 90+ students a year on technical equipment, which is the same patience your posting asks for when assisting other technicians. I learn technical systems fast, I show up, and I would come in ready to work and earn the certifications this trade requires.
I appreciate that you value getting the job done right the first time and creating positive experiences for customers; these are all values that I strive to emulate.
Thank you for taking the time out of your busy day to read my letter. I look forward to the opportunity of doing an interview with you.

On-site field service. Drives a company fleet vehicle to several service locations a day. Weekday schedule, no on-call. Commute from Mesa 85206 is unknown until the employer and shop location are known.

why: Customer service is his strongest point: 5.0-star reviews for over a year. The posting asks techs to 'create positive experiences with customers.'

He has six-plus years of working on his own in the field, through his own company: scheduling jobs, driving to sites, dealing with customers and finishing the work. That is how this job runs day to day.
He is used to job sites. Years of filming construction, trades and industrial sites mean ladders, attics, roofs and hauling 50 to 75 lb gear are routine. He also has a clean driving record.

He has looked after equipment ($30k inventory at ALA, $1M of gear at GCE), which fits 'maintain inventory on service vehicle.' He taught 90+ students a year, which fits 'assist other Service Technicians.'
gaps: The posting requires at least 3 years of HVAC experience and he has none. Answer: 'I don't have HVAC time yet and I won't pretend otherwise. I ran my own field service business for seven years. If service needs more time in the trade, I'd take an install or apprentice spot to learn it right.'
He has no EPA 608 certification (needed to handle refrigerant). Answer: 'Not yet. It's my first step, and it's a few weeks of self-study.' Only say he is working on it once he has actually started.

The job calls for intermediate to advanced troubleshooting of heating, cooling and indoor air quality equipment. Answer: 'I troubleshoot technical equipment on site every week and solve problems without waiting for direction. HVAC diagnostics I'd need to learn properly, and I learn technical systems fast.'

Pay is about $17,000 below his $75,000 floor. Helper or apprentice roles he could realistically start in pay $18 to $22/hr. This is his own decision, not something to raise with the employer. If they ask about pay: 'I know a career change starts lower. My focus is learning the trade the right way.'
reference.gaps_note: Suggested answers carried over from the original analysis. Some assume a course or certification is under way; say those only if they are true when you interview.
reference.jd_source: Copied word for word from the posting Joshua pasted into Claude on 2026-09-16.
reference.jd_text:
Full job description
Starting at $28/hr, our HVAC service technician will possess the knowledge and understanding of how to complete a wide range of HVAC tasks, which includes but is not limited to, routine maintenance & service, installation, troubleshooting & repairing HVAC systems, other miscellaneous home repairs as assigned. These tasks involve a thorough understanding of the proper installation of new HVAC system components, parts and/or equipment in order to facilitate a proper repair. These repairs will be applicable to residential, commercial and light industrial applications.

* *****Sign on Bonus of $2,500 ****
* Quarterly Bonus! You will be eligible for a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings
* No on-call! Weekday schedule!
* The company will provide a tool/equipment allowance of $50 per month
* The company will provide a cell phone allowance of $50 per month
* Company fleet vehicle and fuel card
* Growth opportunities into Lead Technicians and Field Maintenance Managers
* Provided OSHA training
* Competitive hourly rate and corporate-level benefits!

What You'll Do:

* Intermediate to advance skills in troubleshooting all heating, cooling and indoor air quality equipment.
* Independent and self-starting on a wide range of intermediate HVAC service issues, needs and problems.
* Detailed orientation to complete projects and assigned tasks in a timely manner.
* Create positive experiences with customers during all customer interactions.
* Identify/complete any/all additional tasks required to complete the service call in a timely manner.
* Maintain inventory on service vehicle.
* Attend service and safety meetings.
* Drive to multiple service locations each day.
* Responsible for scheduling maintenance/repairs of company service vehicle. including routine maintenance, repairs, and maintaining a clean and well-organized exterior/interior.
* Assist other Service Technicians with questions and troubleshooting.
* Complete the forms required for processing warranty parts.
* Perform other duties as assigned

You Should Have:

* High School diploma or equivalent
* Minimum - 3 years of previous HVAC experience
* Possess a valid state Driver’s License and auto insurance
* Must pass an MVR check to drive a company vehicle
* Ability to climb ladder and enter/exit attic and roof spaces.
* Must be able to lift, push, pull 50lbs regularly; up to 75lbs occasionally; and 75+lbs with assistance.
* #IND1

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

research.overview: The employer for this posting is not named. Joshua pasted the listing text from Indeed (it carries the tag #IND1), and neither the pasted text, the tracker row nor the saved notes include a company name or URL. Without a name there is no way to look up reviews, ratings or employee discussion, so no company research was done. The posting itself describes residential, commercial and light industrial HVAC service, a weekday schedule with no on-call, a company fleet vehicle and fuel card, OSHA training, and growth into Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager roles. It also says the company may use AI tools to review applications and flag 'potential inconsistencies or verification signals.' These are the employer's own claims, not checked against any outside source.
